item.title: Two friends transformed a 225-acre overgrazed Texas ranch, bringing back quail and wildlife
item.description: Two friends, Jim Willis and John Webb, bought a 225-acre overgrazed ranch in Texas in 2000 that could support little beyond cattle. They gradually restored native prairie, planted 3,000 sand plum trees, added a five-acre wetland and changed grazing practices. The work transformed the property into habitat for bobwhite quail, grassland birds, deer, ducks and other wildlife, while also encouraging nearby landowners to join a larger habitat corridor project. Fuente: The Times of India - World.

This organization provides resources and social connections, growing to over 500 members worldwide. Sevah Neuro offers a summer fellowship program with life skills and social activities for children. The student-led initiative also engages in legislative advocacy for greater awareness and resources. Future plans include developing an educational book, a mobile app, and physical learning centers. Fuente: The Times of India - World.

item.title: Meet Jonathan Thai, the 17-year-old whose nonprofit raised $30,000, donated 400 bikes
item.description: After a local retailer slashed community biking programs, a Georgia teenager took action by founding Pedal Forward. This initiative has successfully raised over thirty thousand dollars, providing four hundred bicycles to children in need. Hundreds have benefited from free cycling skills clinics, and the organization's reach is expanding into Tennessee and New York. Now, Pedal Forward is setting its sights internationally, planning humanitarian efforts in Vietnam. Fuente: The Times of India - World.

item.title: In 2009, Washington removed a century-old dike and let tides reclaim 762 acres
item.description: In 2009, the decision to remove sea dikes from the Nisqually River Delta paved the way for a remarkable transformation, rejuvenating 762 acres of marshland. Young Chinook salmon swiftly adapted to the new tidal channels, fostering their feeding and growth. This comprehensive restoration successfully re-established 21 miles of ancestral tidal channels with Puget Sound, showcasing a promising blueprint for coastal resilience in the West Coast regions. Fuente: The Times of India - World.

item.title: Permafrost melt could cost $261 billion in infrastructure damages, study suggests
item.description: A new study provides insight into the economic impact of melting permafrost on Arctic communities. Permafrost covers about 24% of the Northern Hemisphere, including large areas of Alaska, Canada and Siberia. Fuente: Phys.org.
